idiom_name: chained scala.util.chaining.pipe calls over named stages
implementation_notes: scala.util.chaining adds pipe and tap to every type: pipe applies a function to the value and returns the result, so raw.pipe(parse).pipe(validate) reads top to bottom, and Function1's andThen plus Function.chain(fs) build the composed function in the standard library (scala-lang API docs). The chain of pipe calls replaces the classic pipeline object; for sequences, Iterator or LazyList chains give the streaming form, and Future/for-comprehensions the asynchronous one. The stdlib exposes no Pipeline type, which is why this is an idiom rather than a library feature.
pitfalls: pipe has a small runtime overhead compared with a local val and a direct call, so it belongs at pipeline assembly, not inside hot loops.
andThen composes left-to-right while compose is right-to-left; mixing the two silently reverses a chain.
Type inference degrades along long chains of generic stages, so the assembled pipeline usually needs an explicit type ascription.
